title: Conditional 3: Counterfactual Want (я бы выпил, я бы пошёл)
titleRussian: Условное 3: Контрфактическое желание (я бы выпил, я бы пошёл)
description: The 'subject + бы + past' frame on its own (no если-clause) expresses a current desire as a conditional wish. It is the everyday Russian way to say 'I'd have a coffee' or 'I would go for a walk' as a soft, conditional preference.
descriptionRussian: Конструкция «подлежащее + бы + прошедшее» сама по себе (без если-предложения) выражает желание в момент речи как условное. Это самый употребительный способ сказать «я бы выпил кофе» или «я бы пошёл погулять» — мягко, без прямого «хочу».
intro: The same particle again, this time with no if-clause at all. One subject, one past-tense verb, and the particle in between gives you a soft preference rather than a demand. It is the standard answer to being offered something, and it is almost always perfective, because you are naming one specific thing you would do.
rules: Single-clause counterfactual want: subject + бы + past-tense verb. It says 'I would do X' as a soft, conditional preference, with the condition left unstated.
Use the frame in place of 'я хочу + inf' to sound polite or non-pushy; it is the default reply to 'what would you like?'
The past-tense verb agrees with the subject in gender and number: я бы выпил (masc) / выпила (fem) / мы бы выпили (pl). The бы is unstressed and usually sits between subject and verb.

Aspect: almost always perfective. Either one specific bounded action (выпил, пошёл, посмотрел) or a по- verb that packages 'a bit of' an activity into one bounded chunk (поспал, погулял, поговорил - also perfective).
Negative: subject + бы + не + past-tense verb ('Я бы не пошёл туда'). A soft 'no' that leaves room to disagree.
examples: Я бы выпил кофе. (I'd have a coffee.) Masc speaker + pf for one specific cup.
Я бы пошла погулять. (I'd go for a walk.) Fem speaker + pf пошла; погулять is the по- 'for a while' verb, also perfective.
Мы бы посмотрели фильм вечером. (We'd watch a film this evening.) Plural + pf for one specific film.
Антон бы поспал ещё час. (Anton would sleep for another hour.) Specific subject + pf for one bounded nap.
Я бы не стал спорить. (I wouldn't get into an argument.) Negative counterfactual: a soft refusal.
Маша бы пришла к нам в гости в субботу. (Masha would come to visit us on Saturday.) Specific person + pf for one specific visit.

tables.title: Bare want vs counterfactual want
headers: Where you'd use the soft form

rows.label: Я не пойду туда.
cells: Soft no; leaves room for the listener

rows.label: Perfective
cells: one specific bounded action (one cup, one trip, one film)
я бы выпил, я бы пошёл, я бы посмотрел

rows.label: Perfective with по- ('for a while')
cells: 'a bit of' an activity, packaged as one bounded chunk (a short nap, a little walk, a quick chat)
я бы поспал, я бы погулял, я бы поговорил

items.promptEnglish: I (m) would have a coffee, please.
items.hint: Counterfactual want, masc speaker, one cup. бы + past pf form.
items.explanation: The counterfactual-want frame is 'subject + бы + past-tense verb.' Masc speaker + one specific cup → 'я бы выпил.' Выпиваю (impf present) reports a current habit; выпил without бы reports a real past event; хочу выпить is the bare 'I want to drink,' less soft than the бы frame.

items.promptEnglish: Masha would go for a walk in the park.
items.hint: Counterfactual want, fem subject, one walking trip. бы + past pf.
items.explanation: The counterfactual want is 'Маша бы + past pf' → бы пошла (fem of пойти, onset of motion). Идёт (present) and пошла (real past) are both real-event reports without бы. Хочет пойти is the bare 'wants to go,' less soft.

items.promptEnglish: We would watch a film this evening.
items.hint: One specific film, one evening. Plural past, perfective.
items.explanation: The frame uses a past-tense form after бы. Plural pf of посмотреть → посмотрели. The film is one specific event tonight, signalling perfective. Смотрим (present) and посмотрим (pf future) don't fit the бы construction; смотрели (impf past) would describe a process or habit, not the specific evening event.

items.promptEnglish: I (m) would sleep for another hour.
items.hint: A bounded amount of sleep ('one more hour'). Past masc, perfective.
items.explanation: The bounded duration 'ещё час' marks a single bounded nap, signalling perfective поспать. Past masc + бы (already in prompt) → поспал. Сплю is the present (no бы fit); выспался means 'got enough sleep,' a different lexical event; буду спать is the future and does not combine with бы.

items.prompt: На твоём месте я _____ это пальто.
items.promptEnglish: If I were you, I (f) would take this coat.
items.hint: 'На твоём месте' sets up a counterfactual. бы + past pf of взять, fem.
items.explanation: 'На твоём месте' (if I were you) sets up the counterfactual, so the frame is 'я бы + past pf': fem взяла. Беру (present) and возьму (pf future) don't combine with бы; 'бы возьму' is ungrammatical because бы needs a past form, never a future one.

items.promptEnglish: I (f) would have a coffee, to be honest.
items.hint: The counterfactual want: subject + бы + past pf, feminine.
items.explanation: The soft-want frame is subject + бы + past perfective: я бы выпила кофе. Выпил is masculine; выпью is future (бы never takes it); the infinitive cannot carry the frame.

items.promptEnglish: Anton would go for a walk after dinner.
items.explanation: The counterfactual want is бы + past perfective agreeing with the subject: Антон бы пошёл погулять. Пошла is feminine; пойдёт is future; идти an infinitive.

items.prompt: Я _____ на эту лекцию, если честно.
items.promptEnglish: I (m) wouldn't go to that lecture, to be honest.
items.hint: The soft refusal: where do бы and не sit?
items.explanation: The negative frame is subject + бы + не + past verb: я бы не пошёл. Бы comes before the не + verb cluster, never inside it; пойду is future and cannot carry бы.

items.promptEnglish: We would watch this film at the weekend.
items.explanation: The frame agrees in number: мы бы посмотрели. Посмотрим is future (no бы possible); посмотрел is singular; the infinitive cannot serve as the clause's verb.

blanks: Антон бы _____ с тобой об этом в субботу. (Anton would speak with you about that on Saturday.)
Лена бы _____ ещё кусочек торта. (Lena would eat one more slice of cake.)
Мы бы _____ ещё немного в парке. (We would walk a bit more in the park.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The counterfactual-want frame uses a past-tense form after бы, agreeing in gender and number. (1) One specific bounded conversation (one topic, one date) → perfective поговорить, masc → поговорил; говорит (present) does not fit the бы construction. (2) One specific slice → perfective съесть, fem subject Лена → съела; ест (impf present) reports a habit, not a soft want. (3) A little more walking packaged as one bounded chunk → perfective погулять (the по- 'for a while' verb), plural → погуляли; гуляем (present) does not combine with бы.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я бы беру это пальто, оно мне нравится.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I would take this coat; I like it.
errorCorrection.explanation: The counterfactual-want frame is 'subject + бы + PAST-tense verb': взял. Беру is the present ('I am taking, I take'), возьму the perfective future ('I will take'), берёт a present 3sg, none of which combine with бы. For one specific coat, the perfective взял names a single bounded choice, and the бы makes it a soft preference ('I'd take it'), not a real action.

errorCorrection.sentence: На твоём месте я бы покупал эту машину.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: If I were you, I would buy this car.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'На твоём месте' sets up a counterfactual ('if I were you'), and the бы frame uses a past form. For one specific car, the aspect is perfective: купил. The imperfective покупал would frame buying as repeated or ongoing ('would keep buying'), which one specific car rules out. Куплю (future) and покупаю (present) do not combine with бы.

errorCorrection.sentence: Честно говоря, я бы не пойду туда один.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Honestly, I wouldn't go there alone.
errorCorrection.explanation: The negative counterfactual (a soft refusal) is 'subject + бы + не + PAST-tense verb': не пошёл. Пойду is the perfective future ('I will go'), иду the present, пойдёт a future 3sg, and none of these combine with бы. The бы plus the past form turns a categorical 'я не пойду' into the softer, more conversational 'я бы не пошёл'.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) would have a coffee, please. (soft order at a café)
minimalPairs.explanation: A soft café order uses the counterfactual-want frame: 'я бы выпил.' The бы particle plus the past pf form makes the request conversational and non-pushy. Пью is the present tense ('I am drinking / I drink'), a real-time report, not a request.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) would sleep for a bit longer.
minimalPairs.explanation: The bounded duration 'ещё немного' frames a short additional nap, signalling pf поспать → поспал. Выспался means 'got enough sleep' (the result, the state of being well-rested), which the 'ещё немного' framing does not match.

reviewVocab.definition: the one-clause wish frame: a current desire expressed softly as 'subject + бы + past'; the unstated condition is recovered from context
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я бы выпил кофе' конструкция 'я бы выпил' — мягкое выражение желания: говорящий не настаивает.

reviewVocab.definition: soft request (a preference framed with бы to invite agreement rather than to impose; the standard reply pattern to 'what would you like?')
reviewVocab.example: В диалоге 'Что будешь? — Я бы кофе' ответ строится по схеме мягкой просьбы.

reviewVocab.definition: soft refusal (negative counterfactual; 'subject + бы + не + past' offers a non-pushy 'no' that leaves the listener room to disagree)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я бы не пошёл туда' структура смягчает категорическое 'я не пойду'.
